[[Category:Production]]
[[File:Airacobra-p39-assembly-l-oc-02902u.jpg|thumbnail|An assembly plant of the Bell Aircraft Corporation at Wheatfield, New York, USA in the 1940s]]
An '''assembly line''' is a technique of [[production#Production_modes|mass production]] in which the making of products is divided into small, elementary tasks, each to be performed at a '''workstation'''. The products move from workstation to workstation, but labour and machines generally stay at a given workstation.

{{Hidden example}}

<uml>
@startuml
!theme bluegray
title Assembly line — industrial baguette baking
top to bottom direction
skinparam defaultTextAlignment center
skinparam ArrowColor #4A5A63
skinparam rectangle<<machine>> {
  BackgroundColor #DCE3E6
}
skinparam rectangle<<labour>> {
  BackgroundColor #F4F6F7
}

package "Workstation 1 · Dough making" as WS1 {
  together {
    rectangle "Mixer" <<machine>> as M1
    rectangle "Baker 1" <<labour>> as L1
  }
}
package "Workstation 2 · Dividing and shaping dough" as WS2 {
  together {
    rectangle "Divider / shaper" <<machine>> as M2
    rectangle "Baker 2" <<labour>> as L2
  }
}
package "Workstation 3 · Proofing" as WS3 {
  together {
    rectangle "Proofing cabinet" <<machine>> as M3
    rectangle "Baker 3" <<labour>> as L3
  }
}
package "Workstation 4 · Scoring and baking" as WS4 {
  together {
    rectangle "Deck oven" <<machine>> as M4
    rectangle "Baker 4" <<labour>> as L4
  }
}
package "Workstation 5 · Cooling and packing" as WS5 {
  together {
    rectangle "Cooling rack, bagging machine" <<machine>> as M5
    rectangle "Baker 5" <<labour>> as L5
  }
}

rectangle "Finished\nbags of baguettes\nReady to ship!" as OUT

WS1 -down-> WS2 : dough
WS2 -down-> WS3 : shaped loaves
WS3 -down-> WS4 : proved loaves
WS4 -down-> WS5 : baked baguettes
WS5 -down-> OUT : bagged baguettes

@enduml
</uml>

The workpiece (dough becoming baguette) moves down the line from workstation to workstation, while each baker and each machine stay put.
{{End hidden}}
